clue.text: All you want in substitute

parts.note: having your fill is having as much as you want
taken as written

explanation.surface: A request that whoever stands in should simply bring everything you want.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in who covers for someone absent is a temporary replacement, a substitute.

clue.text: The Italian flies around with spirited young girls

indicators.note: around says the insects go round the Italian word

parts.note: taken as written
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian man zooms about with lively girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like a verb but is the plural noun around IL.
explanation.definitionFit: A filly is a young female horse, and colloquially a lively young woman.

clue.text: National emblems mentioned in disclosures

indicators.note: mentioned says the word for disclosures is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: leaks are unauthorised disclosures of information

explanation.surface: Patriotic symbols are referred to in revelations.
explanation.walkthrough: The leek is a national emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable worn on St David's Day is a Welsh national emblem.

clue.text: One's found in one country, then another

indicators.note: found in says the word ones sits inside the first country

parts.note: India is one country
One's read as the word ones, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A traveller discovers a person in one land and then in a second.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a country, so it is the 'another' country after India.

clue.text: Common sayings and how they are perpetuated

explanation.surface: Proverbs, and the means by which they survive.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbial expressions are bywords, and sayings live on through spoken words, 'by words'.

clue.text: Wild horses seen by British on an island in the Med

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for British, as in British Rail
taken as written
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Untamed horses are spotted by a British tourist on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbroken range horses of the American West are wild horses.

clue.text: Expression of admiration I'd included for the bereaved lady

indicators.note: included says the I'd letters are taken inside the exclamation

parts.note: wow expresses admiration
I'd without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A compliment paid to a woman in mourning.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband has died is a bereaved lady.

clue.text: Would-be hero left up end of handle, which reverses the current

indicators.note: would-be suggests the word hero is not quite what it seems, so its letters are rearranged
up in a down clue means the word for left is read upwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of handle

explanation.surface: A wannabe hero goes off to the end of the handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Would-be' turns HERO into RHEO; 'up' reverses PORT to TROP; 'end of' takes E from handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheotrope is an old electrical device, a commutator, that switches the direction of a current.

clue.text: Sad and sore about maternity benefit

indicators.note: about says the word sore surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
MB is an abbreviation for maternity benefit

explanation.surface: A mother is unhappy and annoyed over her maternity pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Maternity benefit was a UK state payment to new mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy or melancholy in mood is a synonym of sad.

clue.text: Storage for six loaded shells?

parts.note: the shells are not ammunition but eggs, each full of yolk and white, kept in half-dozen cartons

explanation.surface: A gun owner wants somewhere to keep half a dozen live cartridges.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardboard carton holding half a dozen eggs stores six filled shells.

clue.text: Hides from which one sees hound go after porkies

indicators.note: after says the dog-and-go pair is placed following the fibs

parts.note: porkies (pork pies) is rhyming slang for lies
a hound is a dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hide from which a watcher spots a hunting dog chasing after lies.
explanation.walkthrough: PORKIES is British rhyming slang: pork pies = lies. 'Hides' is a verb here, not the noun for birdwatchers' shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep still and out of sight is an idiomatic way of saying someone hides.

clue.text: 500 500 sheets of paper — imagine!

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: An exclamation of wonder at a huge pile of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy or picture something in the mind is a synonym of imagine.

clue.text: Memsahib's entering with playwright

indicators.note: with says the answer is held within the words before it, running across them

explanation.surface: A colonial lady makes her entrance accompanied by a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House, a famous playwright.

clue.text: Punter gets around, winning first at a quiet, out-of-the-way place

indicators.note: gets around says the gambler surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a punter is a gambler, someone who backs horses: a backer

indicators.note: first says the win letter comes before the word at

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for win or winning in results tables
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man in a punt makes his way round a sleepy stretch of river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punter' suggests someone poling a punt on a river, which fits the scene, but it is the gambler.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwater is a stagnant side-channel, and figuratively an isolated, sleepy place.

clue.text: Precautionary measures practised by Peter's former partner?

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, so Peter's means the safe's
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Peter's ex-girlfriend apparently took precautions in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name, but in thieves' slang a peter is a safe, as in safecracker.
explanation.definitionFit: Using condoms and similar protection during intercourse is the precaution this phrase names.

clue.text: Amusing, but not at all peculiar

definitions.text: Amusing, but not at all peculiar

parts.words: Amusing, but not at all peculiar
parts.note: plays on the old distinction between funny meaning comic and funny meaning strange

explanation.surface: Something is funny in the comic sense, not the odd sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to specify the comic sense of funny rather than the strange one.

clue.text: Branch rising after a short time

indicators.note: after places the hill after the brief moment

parts.note: sec is short for second, a brief moment
a tor is a rocky hill, a rising of ground

explanation.surface: A tree limb grows upward soon afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads as a verb but is a noun here: TOR, a hill on moorland such as Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of an industry or economy is one division of it, a sector.

clue.text: Blue heeler let loose among domestic pets

indicators.note: among says the jumbled letters go between the two pets

parts.note: the two commonest household pets are cat and dog

indicators.note: loose says the letters of let are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: An Australian dog is let off the lead among household pets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue heeler' sounds like a colour or a shoe, but it is an Australian herding breed; 'loose' makes TLE from the word let.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue heeler is an Australian breed used to herd livestock, a cattle dog.

clue.text: Inn had trouble — being attended to?

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of the two words are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub had problems; is someone dealing with it?
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is under control and being dealt with is described idiomatically this way.

clue.text: Give orders to a court in time

indicators.note: in says the one-and-court letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
a means one, which is I

explanation.surface: Instructions to someone about a court appearance on schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to lay down the law, to give orders with authority.

clue.text: Pioneer New Zealand pilot's flat strips

explanation.surface: A famous aviator's planks of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Batten was a pioneering New Zealand aviator of the 1930s; with 's her surname gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Battens are thin flat lengths of wood used to secure or reinforce, matching flat strips.

clue.text: Beachcomber at first lives on a small island in the bay

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of beachcomber

parts.note: lives means exists, is
a cay is a small low island or reef

explanation.surface: A beachcomber starts out living on an islet in the bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bay of Biscay off France and Spain is the bay meant.

clue.text: Walks vigorously and pants

explanation.surface: Someone marches off briskly and gasps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a verb (breathes hard) but is the noun: strides is Australian and British slang for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strides are long purposeful steps, and also an informal word for trousers.

clue.text: Rub Roger's black eye

parts.note: to shine shoes is to rub them up to a polish
R stands for Roger, the radio word meaning received

explanation.surface: Roger rubs his bruised eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise around the eye from a punch is colloquially called a shiner.

clue.text: Where junkies might dump their needles without worry?

definitions.text: Where junkies might dump their needles without worry?

parts.words: Where junkies might dump their needles without worry?
parts.note: the proverbial needle that can never be found in a big pile of dried grass makes this the safest hiding place for a syringe

explanation.surface: A drug user looks for a safe place to discard used syringes.
explanation.definitionFit: Piles of dried grass are where proverbially no needle can ever be found again.

clue.text: Some of the altos carry on singing something by Puccini

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the choir keeps singing an Italian opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is the Puccini opera, a work sung on stage.

clue.text: At some time in the future? Dead right!

definitions.text: At some time in the future?

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it will happen eventually and is told, quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards or subsequently, at a time yet to come, is a synonym here.

clue.text: Brown has to leave the dance

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone named Brown must quit the ballroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' reads as a surname but is the colour TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is an Argentine ballroom dance.

clue.text: Gets close to one arsonist in prison

indicators.note: in prison says the answer is locked up inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone approaches a fire-raiser who is behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaches or draws close to something is a synonym.

clue.text: A musical group has done badly, given up completely

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the word done are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A pop group performed poorly and threw in the towel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserted or forsaken entirely has been given up altogether.

clue.text: Stir once more on the subject of a watch

parts.note: re means concerning, on the subject of
a wake is a vigil, a watch kept over a body

explanation.surface: A remark about a wristwatch or timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse from sleep again is to stir once more.

clue.text: Temporary shelters one grand, complete with toilets

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
loo is British slang for toilet

explanation.surface: Portable huts cost a thousand, toilets included.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow houses built by Inuit hunters are temporary shelters.
